The Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 is the base law of foreign aid, run largely by the State Department. The Defense Department has its own parallel set of authorities for training and equipping foreign forces, consolidated in Title 10 Chapter 16. Conditions such as the Leahy Laws attach to both. The Global Fragility Act, the Women, Peace, and Security Act, and the Elie Wiesel Act direct strategy toward conflict prevention.

## What you should be able to do

- Compare State Department (Title 22) and Defense Department (Title 10) security assistance.
- Explain how Leahy vetting works and where it applies.
- Describe the strategies the 2017 to 2019 prevention statutes require.

## Reading path

Read these in order. Each card links to the wiki page and to the official text. Ticking a box saves your progress in this browser only.

::: {.reading-card .domain-aid-sanctions data-statute="faa-1961"}
[Foreign Assistance Act](../../statutes/faa-1961.qmd) [1961]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The basic law of U.S. foreign aid. It separated economic from military assistance, set the purposes and conditions of each, and led President Kennedy to create the U.S. Agency for International Development by executive order two months later.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/75/424), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2151?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="faa-1961"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="seccoop-2016"}
[Security Cooperation (Ch. 16)](../../statutes/seccoop-2016.qmd) [2016]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The FY2017 defense authorization gathered dozens of scattered Defense Department authorities for training, equipping, and advising foreign forces into a single chapter of Title 10, with common definitions, oversight, and evaluation rules.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/114/public/328), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/333?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="seccoop-2016"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-aid-sanctions data-statute="leahy-laws"}
[Leahy Laws](../../statutes/leahy-laws.qmd) [1997]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Targeted provision]{.layer-badge}

Two parallel provisions that bar U.S. assistance to any unit of a foreign security force when there is credible information that the unit committed a gross violation of human rights.

[Read it: [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2378d?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="leahy-laws"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-aid-sanctions data-statute="gfa-2019"}
[Global Fragility Act](../../statutes/gfa-2019.qmd) [2019]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

Enacted as Title V of Division J of the Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020. It directs a ten-year, whole-of-government strategy to prevent violent conflict and stabilize fragile states, applied first in a small set of priority countries.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/116/public/94), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/9801?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="gfa-2019"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-aid-sanctions data-statute="wps-2017"}
[Women, Peace & Security Act](../../statutes/wps-2017.qmd) [2017]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

Makes it U.S. policy to promote the meaningful participation of women in conflict prevention, peace negotiations, and post-conflict recovery, and requires a government-wide strategy to carry that out.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/115/public/68), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2152j?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="wps-2017"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-aid-sanctions data-statute="wiesel-2018"}
[Elie Wiesel Act](../../statutes/wiesel-2018.qmd) [2019]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Specific authorization]{.layer-badge}

Declares that preventing genocide and other atrocities is a national interest of the United States and requires the executive branch to organize, train, and report accordingly.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/115/public/441), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2656?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="wiesel-2018"> I have read this</label>
:::

## Further reading

- [Millennium Challenge Act](../../statutes/millennium-challenge-2003.qmd){.subj}: Created the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a small government corporation that gives large, multi-year grants to poor countries that pass a scorecard of governance, economic freedom, and social investment indicators.
- [Foreign Affairs Reform Act](../../statutes/farra-1998.qmd){.subj}: Division G of the FY1999 omnibus appropriations act. It folded the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and the U.S. Information Agency into the State Department and, for the first time, gave USAID a statutory existence as an independent establishment.
- [State Basic Authorities Act](../../statutes/state-basic-1956.qmd){.subj}: The organic statute of the State Department. It sets out the Secretary's management authorities, the department's senior positions, and a long list of operating powers that have been added over the decades.
- [Foreign Service Act](../../statutes/fsa-1980.qmd){.subj}: The personnel law for U.S. diplomats. It establishes a career Foreign Service based on merit, with rank held by the person and not the job, competitive promotion, and worldwide availability.
- [Nunn-Lugar Act](../../statutes/nunn-lugar-1991.qmd){.subj}: Authorized the Defense Department to spend its own funds helping the former Soviet republics secure, transport, and dismantle nuclear, chemical, and other weapons after the Soviet collapse.
- [Mutual Security Act](../../statutes/mutual-security-1951.qmd){.subj}: Merged the Marshall Plan's economic aid, military assistance to allies, and technical assistance into one program under one agency, with the stated purpose of strengthening the free world against Soviet power.
- [Smith-Mundt Act](../../statutes/smith-mundt-1948.qmd){.subj}: The legal foundation of U.S. public diplomacy. It authorized the State Department to explain the United States to foreign audiences through broadcasting, publications, and educational and cultural exchanges.

## Key terms

**Security cooperation**
:   Defense Department activities with foreign security forces, such as training, equipping, and advising, mostly under Title 10 Chapter 16.

**Security assistance**
:   Programs under Title 22, run by the State Department, that provide defense articles, training, and services to foreign governments.

**Leahy vetting**
:   Screening foreign security force units for credible information of gross violations of human rights before they receive U.S. assistance.

## Check yourself

Try to answer each question before opening it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 1. What do the Leahy Laws bar?

U.S. assistance to any unit of a foreign security force when there is credible information that the unit committed a gross violation of human rights. There are two parallel provisions, one for State and one for Defense. See [Leahy Laws](../../statutes/leahy-laws.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 2. What did the FY2017 NDAA do to Defense Department partner authorities?

It gathered dozens of scattered authorities for training, equipping, and advising foreign forces into a single chapter of Title 10, with common definitions, oversight, and evaluation rules. See [Security Cooperation (Ch. 16)](../../statutes/seccoop-2016.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 3. What does the Global Fragility Act direct?

A ten-year, whole-of-government strategy to prevent violent conflict and stabilize fragile states, applied first in a small set of priority countries. See [Global Fragility Act](../../statutes/gfa-2019.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 4. What did the Foreign Assistance Act lead President Kennedy to create?

The U.S. Agency for International Development, by executive order two months after the act. See [Foreign Assistance Act](../../statutes/faa-1961.qmd) and, for USAID's later statutory basis, [Foreign Affairs Reform Act](../../statutes/farra-1998.qmd).
:::
